stem: The constricted region of a chromosome that holds the two sister chromatids together is the
explanation: The centromere (primary constriction) joins sister chromatids and carries the kinetochores, where spindle fibres attach during division. Telomeres are the protective ends of the chromosome.

stem: Meselson and Stahl grew bacteria on heavy nitrogen (¹⁵N) and then on ordinary ¹⁴N. Their results showed that DNA replication is
explanation: After one generation in ¹⁴N all DNA was of intermediate density, so each new molecule had one old and one new strand. Conservative replication would have produced one fully heavy and one fully light band instead.

stem: In the Meselson-Stahl experiment, E. coli with only ¹⁵N-DNA is grown for two generations in a ¹⁴N medium. The DNA then consists of
options: one quarter heavy (¹⁵N-¹⁵N) and three quarters light
explanation: After generation 1 every molecule is hybrid. Each hybrid then separates into one ¹⁵N and one ¹⁴N strand, and both get new ¹⁴N partners, giving one hybrid and one light molecule, so 50 % of each. All hybrid is the result after only one generation.

stem: During DNA replication, the short Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand are joined together by
explanation: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides in the 5′ to 3′ direction, so the lagging strand is made in short pieces; DNA ligase seals the gaps between them. Helicase unwinds the double helix and primase lays down the RNA primers.

stem: A DNA template strand has the base sequence 3′-TACGGA-5′. The mRNA transcribed from it is
explanation: mRNA is complementary and antiparallel to the template: T→A, A→U, C→G, G→C, giving 5′-AUGCCU-3′. 5′-ATGCCT-3′ has the right pairing but contains thymine, which is not found in RNA.

stem: With four different bases read three at a time, the total number of possible codons is
explanation: The number of triplets is 4 × 4 × 4 = 4³ = 64. Of these, 61 code for amino acids and 3 are stop codons, which is why 61 is a tempting wrong answer.

stem: The start codon AUG, which begins translation, codes for the amino acid
explanation: AUG is the initiation codon and also codes for methionine, so most new polypeptides begin with methionine. It is read by the initiator tRNA carrying methionine at the start of translation.

stem: Which of the following mRNA codons does not code for any amino acid and stops translation?
explanation: UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons; no tRNA matches them, so release factors free the polypeptide. AUG is the start codon, GUA codes for valine and UUU for phenylalanine.

stem: Which mutation near the start of a gene is most likely to change every amino acid after it?
options: Substitution of three bases in one codon
explanation: Deleting a single base shifts the reading frame, so every codon downstream is read wrongly (frameshift). A substitution changes at most one codon, and deleting three adjacent bases removes about one amino acid but keeps the frame.

stem: Sickle-cell anaemia results from a point mutation in the gene for the β-chain of haemoglobin, in which
options: valine is replaced by glutamic acid
glutamic acid is replaced by valine
the β-chain is not made at all
explanation: A single base substitution (A to T in the DNA) changes the sixth codon so that valine replaces glutamic acid. The altered haemoglobin crystallises at low oxygen and distorts red cells into sickle shapes.

stem: Down syndrome is caused by
options: the loss of one X chromosome
an extra X chromosome in males
a mutation on the Y chromosome
explanation: Most cases result from non-disjunction during meiosis, giving a gamete with two copies of chromosome 21, so the child has trisomy 21 and 47 chromosomes. Loss of an X gives Turner syndrome and an extra X in males gives Klinefelter syndrome.

stem: During mitosis, sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles in
explanation: At anaphase the centromeres split and the spindle fibres pull the chromatids, now separate chromosomes, to opposite poles. In metaphase they are only lined up at the equator.

stem: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes takes place during
explanation: In prophase I homologous chromosomes pair (synapsis), and non-sister chromatids exchange segments at chiasmata. Homologues are not paired in meiosis II or in mitosis, so crossing over cannot occur there.

stem: DNA is replicated during which phase of the cell cycle?
explanation: S stands for synthesis: each chromosome is copied to form two sister chromatids. G₁ is growth before replication, G₂ is preparation for division, and M is mitosis itself.

stem: A human primary spermatocyte has 46 chromosomes. Each of the two cells formed at the end of meiosis I contains
options: 23 chromosomes, each made of two chromatids
23 chromosomes, each made of one chromatid
46 chromosomes, each made of one chromatid
46 chromosomes, each made of two chromatids
explanation: Meiosis I separates homologous pairs, so the number halves to 23, but sister chromatids stay joined until anaphase II. Single-chromatid chromosomes appear only after meiosis II.

stem: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t). A cross Tt × Tt gives offspring in the phenotypic ratio
explanation: The offspring genotypes are TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1; TT and Tt are both tall, so the phenotype ratio is 3 : 1. The 1 : 1 ratio is from a test cross, Tt × tt.

stem: Bilal crosses a tall pea plant with a dwarf (tt) plant and gets about half tall and half dwarf offspring. The genotype of the tall parent is
options: TT or Tt, which cannot be told apart
explanation: This is a test cross: a TT parent would give all tall (Tt) offspring, while Tt × tt gives Tt and tt in a 1 : 1 ratio. Appearance of dwarf plants shows the tall parent must carry the recessive allele.

stem: In a cross between two pea plants both heterozygous for two independently assorting genes (AaBb × AaBb), the fraction of offspring with the genotype aabb is
explanation: Each gene independently gives aa with probability 1/4 and bb with probability 1/4, so aabb = 1/4 × 1/4 = 1/16. 9/16 is the fraction showing both dominant traits, and 3/16 each of the two mixed classes.

stem: In four o'clock plants, red-flowered (RR) × white-flowered (rr) gives all pink F₁. Selfing the F₁ gives an F₂ phenotypic ratio of
explanation: With incomplete dominance the heterozygote Rr is pink, so each genotype has its own colour and RR : Rr : rr = 1 : 2 : 1 appears directly as 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white. A 3 : 1 ratio would mean red was fully dominant.

stem: A man with blood group A (genotype IAi) and a woman with blood group B (IBi) have a child. The probability that the child has blood group O is
explanation: Group O needs genotype ii, so each parent must pass on i, each with probability 1/2, giving 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. Answering 0 forgets that both parents carry the recessive allele i.

stem: A woman who is a carrier of haemophilia (XᴴXʰ) marries a normal man (XᴴY). The probability that any son of theirs will be haemophilic is
explanation: A son gets his Y from the father and one X from the mother, who passes Xʰ half the time, so each son has a 1/2 chance of being haemophilic. 1/4 is the chance for any child (son or daughter) before the sex is known.

stem: According to Morgan's work on linkage, the frequency of crossing over between two genes on the same chromosome is greater when the genes are
explanation: A chiasma is more likely to form somewhere between two genes the greater the distance between them, so recombination frequency rises with distance; this is the basis of gene mapping. Genes on different chromosomes assort independently rather than by crossing over.
